surprises.head: Utah brought the hits
surprises.body: Utah’s hit score in the close stretches of the game was 204, against their usual 93 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 200 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

surprises.head: A shutout for Karel Vejmelka
surprises.body: Vejmelka stopped all 15 shots, worth 1.7 expected goals. Starting goalies have a night this good about once every 8 starts.

story.head: Vejmelka slams the door on the Blackhawks
paras: An ugly night for the Blackhawks. Anders Lee made his Mammoth debut, after 14 seasons with the Islanders. Dylan Guenther and Michael Carcone scored 40 seconds apart late in the first to put the Mammoth up 2-0. The second was all Mammoth: Nick Schmaltz scored, Lee scored, and Guenther scored his second of the night on the power play to make it 5-0. MacKenzie Weegar and Ryan Donato dropped the gloves early in the third, and Daniil But stretched the lead to 6-0 with just over seven minutes left. Vincent Trocheck made his Mammoth debut, after four seasons with the Rangers, and picked up an assist. Andrew Peeke made his Mammoth debut, after three seasons with the Bruins, and picked up an assist.

The Mammoth drove the play, outshooting the Blackhawks 32-15, and the scoreboard caught up. The Hawks hit three posts, and the bounces never came. Karel Vejmelka turned aside all 15 shots for the Mammoth, and Arvid Söderblom allowed six goals on 32 shots. The Mammoth improved to 1-0-0, tied for first in the NHL in points percentage, while the Blackhawks dropped to 0-2-0, still last in the NHL.
